thread:
sam: Heads up 1: I'm sketching policy for tiered log retention + safe SIEM export. Proposal: keep complete auth/privileged logs for a brief window, then transform to metadata-only for long-term. We need to decide exact windows and export protections (KMS rewrap, approvals).

meera: Sounds reasonable. Quick q: do we differentiate between interactive human admin sessions and automated service tokens? Their forensic usefulness differs.

sam: Yes1 plan is: human-admin full logs 30d, end-user login events 14d, service-accounts 7d. After full tier, records move to hashed/metadata for 1y and then archival strip for 7y.

derek: For exports, recommend a proxy that writes a filtered copy to an export bucket encrypted with a short-lived data key wrapped by our CMK. Only the approver can unwrap using a one-time token. That token expires automatically.

olivia: Good. Add policy that any export >24h TTL requires a second approver and explicit justification text. Also require an RBAC change request template for who can request exports.

sec-bot: notice: export operations must be ticketed. Attach JIRA id to any export artifact.

meera: Implementation detail: do we generate ephemeral keys per-export or rewrap an envelope key per ticket? Which is easier to audit?

derek: Practical flow: 1) authorize via OPA/RBAC 2) export proxy copies filtered objects to export bucket encrypted with ephemeral key 3) ephemeral key wrapped by CMK, with unwrap recorded against ticket. Store audit record with ticket id, requester, approver, unwrap token id, TTL.

iris: Legal hold concern: if legal hold triggers, we must prevent deletion and mark exports immutable; also revoke unwrap tokens if needed. Need a playbook for that.

meera: For SIEM streaming connectors: default should be metadata-only feed. Full-event feeds are opt-in with strict onboarding (contract + 2 approvers) and shorter retention on the receiving side.

sam: Let's publish connector types: metadata-only (default) and full-event (restricted). Also include automated PII masking unless explicit forensics flag is present.

olivia: Operational controls: who can create ephemeral keys? Limit to a service principal and audit all key-creation ops. Document CMK rotation and key versioning so old unwrap tokens can still be validated where needed.

derek: Add a redaction_profile field to export config so we can select masking pipelines per compliance regime (PCI/PII/General).

meera: Incident response: allow emergency access path that bypasses normal approvers but logs to tamper-evident audit trail, notifies legal/CISO, and auto-expires (e.g., 1 hour).

iris: Also add requirement that any RBAC change that enables exportable fields include sample queries and an explicit justification for auditors.

sam: Draft export proxy snippet I mocked up: ```yaml
export:
  ticket_required: true
  secondary_approver_for_ttl_gt_hours: 24
  mask_default: true
  redaction_profile: "general"
  allowed_principals: ["human-admin", "security-team"]
  ephemeral_key_ttl_seconds: 3600
  audit_store: "kms-wrapped-metadata"
```

derek: I'll produce a sequence diagram for unwrap flow.

olivia: I'll write the RBAC-change template and sample justification.

iris: I'll loop in legal on hold language and comment on retention durations.

meera: I'll compile vuln triage use-cases so we don't over-retain raw payloads unnecessarily.

sam: Action items: build RFC with retention matrix by principal, SIEM connector types, export proxy behavior (ephemeral KMS rewrap), RBAC template for export requests, emergency bypass playbook. Please review and add comments by EOD Friday.

sam: FYI: incident-bot will kick off a checklist if export path is used in a live incident. Make sure runbook references are attached to tickets. :thumbsup:
